```{r}
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))
```
# Exploring the clinical data

```{r}
clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(sex, status) |> 
  count() |>
  group_by(sex) |> 
  mutate(percentage = (n/sum(n))*100)
```
The patients to which the data relates to are about two thirds men to one third women, with roughly 50% survival rate, though survival of women is sligthly lower than that of men.

```{r}
clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(cancer_type, sex) |> 
  count() |>
  group_by(cancer_type) |> 
  mutate(affects_both_sex = if_else(n()>1,
                                    TRUE,
                                    FALSE)) |>
  View()
```
The data collected to 11 types of cancer, two of which (breast cancer and skin cancer) affect only women or men respectively.

```{r}
clinical_augment |> 
  filter(status == "DECEASED") |> 
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarise(average_survival_months = mean(os_months)) |> 
  arrange(average_survival_months)
```
# Exploring the types of mutations (which genes, where in the genome)
```{r}
mutation_augment |> 
  group_by(hugo_symbol) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = hugo_symbol))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = "Number of mutations associated to genes",
       x = "Hugo symbol of affected gene",
       y = "Number of mutations")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45,
    hjust = 1
  ))
```
```{r}
clinical_muation <- mutation_augment |> 
                        full_join(clinical_augment)
mutation_augment |> 
  group_by(hugo_symbol, cancer_type) |> 
  count() |> 
  arrange(desc(n))
```
There are big variations in the number of genes with mutations. Some genes are only affected once, other multiple times.  

```{r}
mutation_augment |> 
  group_by(hugo_symbol) |> 
  count(name = "nbr_occurences") |>
  ungroup() |> 
  summarise(average_mean(nbr_occurences))
```
